own_solution.law: Continuity gives v2 = 4v1. The manometer gives dp = (rho_m - rho)g dh = 14817.6 Pa. Horizontal Bernoulli gives dp = 15rho v1^2/2, hence Q = (pi d1^2/4)sqrt[2dp/(15rho)] = 0.0110395 m³/s.
assumptions: The manometer is in hydrostatic equilibrium when read.
The stated steady, incompressible, frictionless flow model applies.
The replacement statements specify which manometer liquid is present at the stated reading.
Replacements confined to an earlier experiment leave the present measurement unchanged.

defect_reasons.other: The K claims incorrectly turn an absolute-pressure feasibility constraint into a different flow law outside q > dp, replacing the measured pressure difference by q without physical justification.

counterexamples: At the authors' counter-regime value q = 5 kPa, the stated manometer reading still requires dp = 14817.6 Pa and therefore p2 = -9817.6 Pa; the proposed reference expression instead gives Q = 6.41275 L/s, corresponding to dp = 5000 Pa and a manometer difference of about 4.049 cm, contradicting the stated 12 cm.
notes: All certified numerical answers at listed values are correct, including 2.38885, 3.80898 and 4.50684 L/s for replacement densities 1590, 2500 and 3100 kg/m³. The primary relations, dimensional conversions, disconnected attachments and elevation cancellations are correct. Absolute pressure cancels from Bernoulli: q > dp checks positive throat pressure but does not establish an alternative answer when that condition fails. If another flow regime occurs, additional physics and compatibility with the measured manometer reading must be addressed; the supplied outside-regime expression does neither. I retain the pass-1 C assignments for absolute pressure. I retract the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag because pass 2 explicitly identifies the numeral-free sentences as controls rather than the claimed numerical minimal pairs. Both explicitly claimed numerical minimal pairs preserve their number and unit and change the intended attachment or timing. equation_consistent is false because of the outside-regime reference expressions; the main Venturi equations are consistent.
